topics.title: Time - analogue: Read and represent time to the hour and past the hour; time to the nearest minute

questions.stem: The minute hand counts \(60\) minutes every hour, and each number on the clock represents a span of \(5\) minutes. In a, how many minutes does it take for the minute hand to move from \(12\) to \(1\)?

questions.hint: Count how many number spaces the minute hand moves from \(12\) to \(1\) (\(1\)), then multiply by \(5\) minutes per space.

keyPoints.note: Moving from 12 to 1 is 1 number space(s). Since each space is 5 minutes, multiply 1 × 5.

questions.solution: Moving from \(12\) to \(1\) is \(1\) number spaces of \(5\) minutes each, which takes \(1 \times 5 = 5\) minutes.

steps.explain: Locate the starting number \(12\) and the ending number \(1\) on the clock face (highlighted in yellow).

questions.hint: Count how many number spaces the minute hand moves from \(12\) to \(2\) (\(2\)), then multiply by \(5\) minutes per space.

keyPoints.note: Moving from 12 to 2 is 2 number space(s). Since each space is 5 minutes, multiply 2 × 5.

questions.solution: Moving from \(12\) to \(2\) is \(2\) number spaces of \(5\) minutes each, which takes \(2 \times 5 = 10\) minutes.

questions.hint: Count how many number spaces the minute hand moves from \(12\) to \(4\) (\(4\)), then multiply by \(5\) minutes per space.

keyPoints.note: Moving from 12 to 4 is 4 number space(s). Since each space is 5 minutes, multiply 4 × 5.

questions.solution: Moving from \(12\) to \(4\) is \(4\) number spaces of \(5\) minutes each, which takes \(4 \times 5 = 20\) minutes.

questions.stem: The minute hand counts \(60\) minutes every hour, and each number on the clock represents a span of \(5\) minutes. In f, how many minutes does it take for the minute hand to move from \(2\) to \(3\)?

questions.solution: Moving from \(2\) to \(3\) is \(1\) number spaces of \(5\) minutes each, which takes \(1 \times 5 = 5\) minutes.

questions.stem: The minute hand counts \(60\) minutes every hour, and each number on the clock represents a span of \(5\) minutes. In h, how many minutes does it take for the minute hand to move from \(5\) to \(8\)?

questions.hint: Count how many number spaces the minute hand moves from \(5\) to \(8\) (\(3\)), then multiply by \(5\) minutes per space.

keyPoints.note: Moving from 5 to 8 is 3 number space(s). Since each space is 5 minutes, multiply 3 × 5.

questions.solution: Moving from \(5\) to \(8\) is \(3\) number spaces of \(5\) minutes each, which takes \(3 \times 5 = 15\) minutes.

questions.stem: The minute hand counts \(60\) minutes every hour, and each number on the clock represents a span of \(5\) minutes. In j, how many minutes does it take for the minute hand to move from \(8\) to \(12\)?

questions.hint: Count how many number spaces the minute hand moves from \(8\) to \(12\) (\(4\)), then multiply by \(5\) minutes per space.

keyPoints.note: Moving from 8 to 12 is 4 number space(s). Since each space is 5 minutes, multiply 4 × 5.

questions.solution: Moving from \(8\) to \(12\) is \(4\) number spaces of \(5\) minutes each, which takes \(4 \times 5 = 20\) minutes.

keyPoints.note: Each clock number is 5 minutes. Count 10 minutes clockwise from 12.

questions.solution: To show \(10\text{ past }12\), the minute hand must be pointing to the 2 (10 minutes past 12).

steps.explain: Read the target time on watch b: \(10\text{ past }12\) means \(10\) minutes past \(12\text{ o'clock}\).

questions.hint: Start at \(12\) (\(0\) minutes) and count clockwise by \(5\)s for each clock number (and by \(1\)s for individual minute marks) to reach \(30\) minutes.

keyPoints.note: Each clock number is 5 minutes. Count 30 minutes clockwise from 12.

questions.solution: To show \(\dfrac{1}{2}\text{ past }12\), the minute hand must be pointing to the 6 (30 minutes past 12).

steps.explain: Read the target time on watch d: \(\dfrac{1}{2}\text{ past }12\) means \(30\) minutes past \(12\text{ o'clock}\).

keyPoints.note: Each clock number is 5 minutes. Count 0 minutes clockwise from 12.

questions.solution: To show \(12\text{ o'clock}\), the minute hand must be pointing to the 12 (0 minutes past 12).

steps.explain: Read the target time on watch f: \(12\text{ o'clock}\) means \(0\) minutes past \(12\text{ o'clock}\).

topics.title: Time - units: Seconds, minutes, hours and days; duration of events

questions.stem: How many minutes does it take the hour hand to move from one number to the next on a clock?
questions.hint: Careful! The question asks about the hour hand, not the minute hand. Moving from one hour number to the next (for example, from \(1\) to \(2\)) is \(1\) full hour.

keyPoints.text: hour hand to move from one number to the next
keyPoints.note: The hour hand takes 1 full hour to move from one number to the next, and 1 hour = 60 minutes.

questions.solution: The hour hand moves from one number to the next in \(1\) hour, which is \(60\text{ minutes}\).

steps.explain: Read the question carefully: it asks about the hour hand (which shows hours), not the minute hand.
While the hour hand moves from one number to the next (such as from \(12\) to \(1\)), the minute hand travels all the way around the clock face once.
steps.work: \(1\text{ full turn of the minute hand} = 60\text{ minutes}\)

steps.explain: Convert \(1\) hour into minutes: \(1\text{ hour} = 60\text{ minutes}\) (whereas \(5\) minutes is for the minute hand).
Therefore, it takes the hour hand \(60\text{ minutes}\) to move from one number to the next.
